headline: COPPER LOGS WORST LOSING STREAK SINCE 2021 — Fifth Consecutive Week of Declines as AI Demand Narrative Collapses
snippet: Copper suffered its fifth consecutive week of price declines as of November 13 — its longest losing streak since 2021 — driven by weakening sentiment around AI data-centre build-out timelines and a firmer US dollar following hot CPI data. The streak wipes out months of gains and represents a structural reassessment of copper's AI demand premium, with LME copper now down more than 15% from its September record high.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD Q3 DISAPPOINTS: Output Tracks Low-End of Guidance, Costs Near Top — Shares Slide Nov 13
snippet: Equinox Gold (NYSE: EQX) fell on November 13 after Q3 2026 results showed production tracking toward the low end of full-year guidance while all-in sustaining costs approached the top of the guidance range — the dual squeeze that hits gold mining margins hardest. One analyst trimmed a price target in response, and the stock's underperformance relative to gold's modest recovery on the same day highlights the ongoing cost-inflation challenge hitting mid-tier producers.

headline: FIRST ATLANTIC NICKEL OPENS SECOND AWARUITE ZONE — 1.3 km Strike at Alloy Max North, Up to 504m Drill Intersections (TSXV: FAN)
snippet: First Atlantic Nickel (TSXV: FAN) confirmed a second large-scale awaruite (nickel-iron-cobalt alloy) zone at its Alloy Max North discovery in Newfoundland, with three drill holes returning magnetically recoverable awaruite across 1.3 km of strike at depths of 405–504 metres. The zone sits 7 km north of the original RPM Zone within FAN's 30 km Pipestone XL Trend, suggesting district-scale potential for a type of nickel deposit amenable to bulk, low-cost magnetic separation extraction rather than conventional sulphide processing.

headline: INDIA BANS LITHIUM BATTERY BLACK MASS EXPORTS — $300M Critical Minerals Policy Cuts Recycling Flows to China
snippet: India banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass — the recycled material containing lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese — on November 11, as part of a government policy backed by approximately $300 million in incentives to reduce reliance on China-dominated critical mineral supply chains. The move is designed to retain value-added processing onshore and is expected to redirect significant black mass tonnages toward India's domestic battery recycling industry, cutting Chinese processors' access to affordable feedstock.

headline: RARE EARTH STOCKS EXTEND RALLY NOV 13 — USAR +3%, MP Materials +2%, Critical Metals +3% as China Trade Noise Fades
snippet: Rare earth stocks extended their recovery on November 13 with USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) climbing 3%, MP Materials (NYSE: MP) gaining 2%, and Critical Metals Corp (Nasdaq: CRML) adding 3%, as the sector continued rebounding from USAR's sharp 11% drop on November 10 following a Q3 revenue miss. The stabilization follows the November 10 expiry of China's formal rare earth export pause — which ended without escalation — reducing a key headline risk that had amplified post-earnings selling pressure across the group.

headline: VAULT SHAREHOLDERS VOTE 99.74% YES ON GENESIS MERGER — Australian Gold Consolidation On Track for Nov 26 Close
snippet: Vault Minerals shareholders voted 99.74% in favour of its merger with Genesis Minerals at a scheme meeting on November 11, bringing Australia's most closely watched gold mining consolidation to its final judicial hurdle — a court approval hearing set for November 16 — before an expected implementation date of November 26. The combined company is projected to become a top-10 Australian gold producer by output, with Genesis contributing its Leonora Operations and Vault adding the Lady Bountiful and Meekatharra assets.

headline: NVRO METALS BANKS $35M, TARGETS NORTHERN TERRITORIES ACQUISITION — Junior Grows Through Canada's Critical Mineral Corridor
snippet: NVRO Metals closed a $35 million private placement (approximately US$24.57 million) on November 11 to fund the acquisition of Northern Territories Resources, adding a Northern Canada critical mineral asset to its portfolio. The raise positions NVRO — a small-cap TSX-listed company — as a consolidator in Canada's Northern mineral corridor at a time when government incentives under Canada's Critical Minerals Strategy are lowering financing thresholds for Northern projects with strategic mineral content.

headline: SUPPLY GROWTH WON'T SAVE COPPER FROM SQUEEZE: FXStreet Flags Structural Deficit Risk Through 2027 Despite New Mines
snippet: FXStreet's November 12 deep-dive argues that projected copper mine supply growth through 2026-2027 will likely be insufficient to prevent a structural market squeeze, as project delays, permitting backlogs and rising capex continue to erode pipeline confidence. The analysis contends that the current futures-driven correction — now in its fifth week — is creating a disconnection from physical market fundamentals, particularly given near-historic low Shanghai inventories, and may be setting up a sharper eventual rebalancing than consensus models assume.

headline: GOLD MINERS FALL 3X HARDER THAN GOLD — Why the Operating Leverage Cuts Both Ways, and When the Snapback Historically Hits
snippet: A November 2026 Discovery Alert analysis unpacks why gold mining stocks consistently sell off 2–3x harder than bullion during corrections — operating leverage amplifies every dollar change in gold price into outsized EPS swings at mid-tier producers — and argues that the current 30–40% drawdown from 2026 highs in the GDXJ while gold is off only ~12% from its year high represents the historical setup that has preceded the most powerful sector recoveries. The piece outlines the technical conditions that have flagged prior cycle bottoms.

headline: COPPER +15.6% YTD vs OIL -7.6%: Averin Maps the Commodity Supercycle Splits — Copper Leads as Lithium and Crude Diverge
snippet: Ruslan Averin's November 2026 commodity performance report shows copper holding a 15.6% year-to-date gain despite its recent five-week drawdown, while Brent crude is down 7.6% year-to-date on renewed Iran nuclear talks, and lithium remains deeply depressed. The divergence between copper's supply-deficit fundamentals and the broader macro-driven correction is the central tension for commodity investors entering Q4 2026, with the data arguing copper's near-term weakness is a correction within a larger structural uptrend rather than a trend reversal.

headline: CONTANGO SILVER & GOLD Q3: Manh Choh Ore Tons Up 16% QoQ — NYSE American CTGO Posts Quarterly Production Update
snippet: Contango Silver & Gold (NYSE American: CTGO) reported Q3 2026 results for the quarter ended September 30, with ore tons mined at its Manh Choh gold project in Alaska up approximately 16% quarter-over-quarter, reflecting continued ramp-up progress at the Kinross joint-venture mine. Manh Choh is the company's primary production driver as it advances its Tri-State silver asset in Colorado toward feasibility study — making this quarterly improvement a key data point in CTGO's transition from explorer to junior producer.
